name: Deploy Adapter
purpose: The one project module that talks to the deploy vendor. Wraps the vendor's CLI (or SDK) behind a fixed named-verb surface every other module imports. Uploads versions, promotes versions, lists version history, resolves the newest-of-main from the preview alias, and describes any single version's provenance and URLs. Nothing else in the project spawns the vendor CLI or issues a vendor deploy call.
responsibilities: Expose `uploadVersion({ previewAlias })` that uploads the current build to the vendor and returns `{ versionId, versionIdUrl, previewAliasUrl }`; refuse an empty `previewAlias` with `DEPLOY_PREVIEW_ALIAS_REQUIRED` (AC-12102-2, AC-12103-1).

Expose `promoteVersion({ versionId })` that routes production traffic to the named version and returns `{ promotedVersionId, previousVersionId }`; refuse when `versionId` is absent from `listVersions()` with `DEPLOY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND` (AC-12102-3, AC-12108-3).
Expose `listVersions()` returning the recent version history with the currently-serving id marked (AC-12109-1).
Expose `resolveNewestOfMain()` that looks up the version id currently behind the operator-chosen preview alias and returns it (AC-12108-2).
Expose `describeVersion({ versionId })` returning provenance (`versionSha`, `builtAt`, `ciRunUrl`) and URLs (`versionIdUrl`) for the named version (AC-12112-1, AC-12112-2).
Refuse a manifest whose production route resolves to the same host as the preview alias URL with `DEPLOY_URL_COLLAPSED` (AC-12105-2).
Route every CLI invocation through a redactor that scrubs the vendor API token and account id from every emitted log line (AC-12107-3, AC-12106-2).
internalStructure: One stateless class per process with an injected vendor binding and an injected redactor. The vendor binding is a project-authored module implementing the port in the interfaces block; the default vendor binding shells to the `wrangler` CLI and lives under the same package as the adapter. Every verb is a thin translation from the named surface to a vendor CLI invocation (or SDK call) plus response parsing plus provenance-URL assembly.

interfaces.name: vendorBinding
interfaces.description: Project-supplied vendor binding implementing `uploadArtefact({ configPath, previewAlias })`, `deployVersion({ versionId })`, `listVersions()`, `getAlias({ alias })`. The default binding shells to `wrangler versions upload --preview-alias <alias>`, `wrangler versions deploy <versionId>`, `wrangler versions list`, and `wrangler versions view <alias>` respectively.

interfaces.name: redactor
interfaces.description: Log-line filter that replaces any bytes matching the vendor API token or account id with a fixed placeholder before emitting; runs on every stdout and stderr line the vendor CLI produces.

interfaces.name: manifest
interfaces.description: The wrangler-manifest loader (TAC-1302) resolving the current Worker's config, the production route or custom-domain declaration, and the declared binding names.

dependencies.name: Wrangler Manifest
dependencies.description: Upstream source of the config the adapter passes to the vendor CLI, and the manifest the collapsed-URL guard reads.

dependencies.name: Preview URL Resolver
dependencies.description: Assembles the preview alias URL and version-id URL strings the adapter returns; consulted from `uploadVersion` and `describeVersion`.

tradeoffs: The adapter is process-local and stateless; every call reaches the vendor. That means a chain of adapter calls in one CI step costs one vendor round-trip per call rather than a shared session. The trade keeps the adapter easy to reason about and easy to reimplement against a different vendor. A project that wants a session-shared invocation supplies a vendor binding whose backing is a long-lived process rather than a CLI spawn per call; the port shape does not change.
